doc.title: Genevieve Rose interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 14, 1998

chapter: Taking up bass and high school
title: Gradual switch to bass and her mother's support
summary: She moved to bass gradually, decided to focus on it by senior year, and her mother supported and drove her everywhere.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Well let me see if you can remember the first time you came home from high school and told your mother that you were now going to be playing the acoustic bass. Was she familiar with what that instrument really was?

Oh yes well because I had — well I didn’t actually just switch, you know. I didn’t say I’m playing guitar today and tomorrow I’m playing bass. It was gradual. So I just kind of played bass on the side. I also played, when I was in high school, a year I did bassoon, I played baritone horn in the marching band. I did a lot of different instruments, and bass was just one of them. And so it was really gradual. And it wasn’t until like maybe my senior year of high school that I actually decided that I was going to concentrate on the

bass. Because up until that point I was doing so much guitar work, and I hadn’t had any formal lessons on the bass, you know I’d just basically taught myself, so like my technique wasn’t really great or anything. But I started finding more and more opportunities. I was playing, I was enjoying it more, and I really liked the style of music that I was able to improvise and put in my own voice to the music. And so it was just gradual. And my mother’s been always very supportive of whatever instrument that I wanted to play. And I think that she’s happy as long as I’m happy. And I really enjoyed being able to put my own self into the playing, into the music, through improvisation.
How does she feel about you being in these New York City nightclubs?

Oh she loves it. Well she drove me down there so I wouldn’t have to leave my car down there. But she is very supportive of everything. And for a long time, when I first started I didn’t have a vehicle, she was chauffeuring me to every performance and rehearsal, so—
She was a jazz mom, not a soccer mom.
Yup. It was like her full time job for a while.
